The image shows a single leaf that is:
- Completely brown/desiccated with a dried, dead appearance
- Curled and twisted along its length
- Uniformly necrotic with no green tissue remaining
- No powdery coating, no sooty black surface, no discrete lesions

This pattern of complete leaf desiccation, curling, and dieback is characteristic of **Die_Back** — a condition where the tissue progressively dies from the tip/margins inward, resulting in complete leaf death and curling/shriveling. There are no discrete anthracnose lesions (irregular dark spots with defined margins), no white powdery coating (Powdery Mildew), and no black sooty surface layer (Sooty Mould).
